Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

qio (development version)

  • bloom_filter_may_contain() no longer reports FALSE, “definitely absent”, for values that are present. bit64::integer64 values are hashed exactly, and unsigned columns are checked by their stored bit pattern. A fraction, an out-of-range value, or a classed value such as a factor or POSIXct is now an error instead of a FALSE (#43).
  • Fixed write_parquet(append = TRUE) leaving the original file unreadable when the append failed with an error after writing its first new row group (#34). An error during an append now leaves the file as it was, and "bytes"-encoded strings in columns, names, metadata or crs are refused before any file is touched.
  • An explicit INT32 column no longer writes -2147483648 as a missing value. That value is R’s integer NA, so it is now refused like any other out-of-range value, and the error names the row and the value (#38).
  • write_parquet() writes a list of raw vectors as a binary (BYTE_ARRAY) column, with NULL for a missing value, and parquet_schema() declares it as "BINARY", "GEOMETRY" or "GEOGRAPHY". The geospatial types hold well-known binary with a crs (and, for GEOGRAPHY, an edge algorithm), and qio records each column chunk’s geospatial statistics.
  • geospatial_statistics() reports the bounding box and geometry types of every GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY column chunk, so readers can choose row groups by box before reading data.
  • Fixed the vendored carquet writer recording, for every row group after the first, geospatial statistics that included the earlier row groups.
  • schema() reports a GEOMETRY or GEOGRAPHY CRS whole however long it is. Files that put inline PROJJSON there, as DuckDB does, had it cut to 127 bytes.

qio 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-09-29

  • Fixed undefined behavior reported by CRAN’s sanitizer checks (M1-SAN, clang-UBSAN and gcc-UBSAN). Batch reads no longer load integer and floating-point values through misaligned pointers, and writing a string column that contains empty strings no longer passes a NULL pointer to memcmp() or memcpy(). Results were already correct; only the undefined behavior is removed.
